title: Terraform deployment assertions and apply-safety guard for VPC/private installs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a hardened CI/CD flow for Terraform-based Private (VPC) deployments that combines linting, policy-as-code gating, plan analysis, and an apply-safety guard. Goals: (1) prevent unsafe changes to networking/KMS/IAM and cross-account bindings, (2) enable canary workspace rollouts for module upgrades, and (3) produce machine-readable plan artifacts and annotated GitHub checks for security and SRE review. This ticket covers pipeline definitions, OPA/Conftest policy packaging, plan artifact storage, approval rules, and health-check hooks post-apply.
acceptance_criteria: CI validates all Terraform modules with terraform fmt/validate and tflint in PRs
Plan stage produces JSON plan artifact and policy evaluation result attached to GitHub Check
OPA/Rego and Conftest checks run against plan JSON and block apply when policy score >= threshold
Apply requires manual approval for changes touching: aws_kms_key, aws_iam_role, aws_vpc, route tables, peering, and security groups with wide egress/ingress
Canary workspaces execute module upgrades on a reserved staging VPC and run automated health checks (smoke infra tests) before promoting
Plan diff analyzer flags resource replacements and data-loss risks and surfaces to PR body
Plan artifacts stored in signed S3 path with retention and access logs for audit
implementation_notes: Pipeline steps: checkout -> tfenv setup -> terraform init -> fmt/validate -> tflint -> terraform plan -out plan.binary -> terraform show -json plan.binary > plan.json -> run conftest/opa against plan.json -> upload plan.json and policy report -> create GitHub check with summary
Use OPA rego rules for high-level guards (no public S3, no overly permissive SGs, mandatory kms encryption), and Conftest for provider-level schema assertions where rego is verbose
Introduce a policy scoring heuristic: block if any critical policy fails OR if cumulative score >= 5 (configurable), to balance strict enforcement and developer velocity
Implement an apply-safety step that enforces an approval gate in GitHub Checks for any change flagged as high-impact; approvals must come from 2 approvers: approver group includes SRE and Security

Canary workspaces will be instantiated using dedicated workspace naming convention: canary/<branch>/<module>@<version>; success triggers automated promotion job that runs plan-only against production workspace
Health checks post-apply: run Terratest-like suite (status of NAT gateways, route propagation, KMS key policy attachments, service endpoints) and upload results to infra-monitoring dashboard
Store plan artifacts and policy reports in s3://redwood-iac-plans/<env>/<repo>/<pr>/<plan-id>/ with signed URLs exposed in the GitHub Check
Integrate with existing OPA policy-repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/opa-policies) and add a new folder for private/vpc-rego
Add telemetry for policy failures and gating rates to Console observability (per-project rate of blocked applies)
Failure modes: if policy evaluation service times out, pipeline should fail closed and notify on-call via PagerDuty
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly strict policies block day-to-day work. Mitigation: start with warn-only mode for non-critical rules and ship a policy dashboard for rapid tuning.

Risk: Storing plan artifacts increases sensitive data footprint. Mitigation: redact values marked sensitive in Terraform before upload and use short-lived signed URLs plus bucket encryption and access logging.
Risk: Canary workspaces might diverge from production due to different inputs. Mitigation: canonicalize inputs via a shared canary-params module and surface input drift in promotion step.
Risk: Long-running policy scans add pipeline latency. Mitigation: run fast preflight (subset of critical rules) and longer background evaluation with eventual blocking for high-risk diffs.
Risk: Approval bottleneck slows releases. Mitigation: allow auto-approve for low-risk label sets and use scheduled windows for large infra changes
